```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5)
library(data.table)
raw <- fread("loggers/q3_all_stations.csv")
qc <- readRDS("loggers/q3_qc_flags.rds")
```

# Summary

Six stations were active in Q3. Between them they logged
`r format(nrow(raw), big.mark = ",")` fifteen-minute readings of stage,
water temperature and conductivity. After automatic and manual QC,
`r round(100 * mean(qc$flag == "ok"), 1)`% of readings were accepted
without modification.

# Station status

| Station | Location             | Status        | Gaps (h) |
|---------|----------------------|---------------|---------:|
| S01     | Upper weir           | OK            |        0 |
| S02     | Footbridge           | OK            |        3 |
| S03     | Confluence           | Battery fault |      142 |
| S04     | Mill race            | OK            |        0 |
| S05     | Lower ford           | Silted        |       18 |
| S06     | Estuary limit        | OK            |        6 |

# QC procedure

Each reading was checked in this order:

1. **Range check.** Values outside physically plausible bounds were
   flagged. The bounds are stored per station:

   ```{r bounds, echo=TRUE}
   bounds <- fread("config/station_bounds.csv")
   bounds[station %in% c("S03", "S05")]
   ```

2. **Spike check.** A reading differing from both neighbours by more
   than three times the rolling MAD was flagged as a spike.

   ```{r spikes, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
   raw[, mad := frollapply(stage, 9, mad, align = "center"), by = station]
   raw[, spike := abs(stage - shift(stage)) > 3 * mad &
                  abs(stage - shift(stage, -1)) > 3 * mad]
   ```

3. **Flatline check.** Six or more identical consecutive readings were
   flagged.
4. **Manual review.** Flagged periods were plotted and reviewed by
   eye; the reviewer could accept, correct or reject each one.

# Station S03

The S03 logger lost power on 11 August. The replacement battery was
fitted on 17 August, giving a gap of about six days. We have not
attempted to fill it.

```{r fig-s03, fig.cap="Stage at S03 around the battery fault. Shaded area: no data."}
s03 <- raw[station == "S03" & between(time, as.POSIXct("2024-08-05"), as.POSIXct("2024-08-24"))]
plot(s03$time, s03$stage, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "Stage (m)")
rect(as.POSIXct("2024-08-11"), -10, as.POSIXct("2024-08-17"), 10,
     col = adjustcolor("grey", 0.4), border = NA)
```

# Station S05

S05 shows a gradual upward drift in stage from mid-July which is not
matched at S04 or S06. On the site visit on 2 September the sensor was
found partly buried in silt. Readings from 15 July to 2 September have
been flagged as *suspect*, not rejected; the drift is small (about
4 cm) and a correction may be possible later.

# Conductivity

Conductivity readings are temperature-compensated to 25 °C using

$$
\kappa_{25} = \frac{\kappa_T}{1 + a\,(T - 25)}
$$

with $a = 0.0191$ per °C. The coefficient was checked against lab
measurements of grab samples in July and found adequate.

# Actions

- Replace the S03 battery pack with the higher-capacity model before
  winter.
- Move the S05 sensor about 30 cm upstream, out of the silt trap.
- Ask the data manager (data.manager@example.org) to push the QC'd
  series to the public portal.
